1.sofaString: 99	Pt, *****, is a 2 month old female who is diagnosed with heart block with progressive heart failure who is now being referred for heart transplant psychosocial assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's mother and father and review of the medical records.   SW spent 45 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, *****, lives with her parents in ** *********, *******.  They reside at **** ****** ** 208, ** *********, **  *****.  They reside in a single dwelling home.  They live in * **** with well water and central heating and a/c.  They have a filter on the water, but use bottled water for drinking.  They have 2 cats.  There is no smoking in the home.           Demographics:  Mother: ******* ******  DOB:  **/**/****           Age:  25  Employment:  9th grade English teacher for ** **** ****** School District (currently on leave until ******)  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ***** ******  DOB:  **/**/****    Age:  27  Employment:  ****** *******   *****:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Support systems:  Both parents disclose that they provide support to one another.  Currently, mom has been staying here with ***** and dad has been going back and forth between home and here in order to keep working.  Mom had been staying in the home of a friend locally overnight.  However, the home she was staying in was on the market and recently sold.  The parents had been looking into finding somewhere to **** on a month to month basis but have not been successful in this.  However, they have another friend locally that they can stay with.  ******* is trying to decide if she will do that or if she will get on the list for ****** ******** *****. She disclosed she tried staying at bedside here at the hospital one night, but was unable to sleep and found that she had poor coping skills the next day due to the lack of sleep.         ******* disclosed that her parents reside in ***** *******.  ***** states that his family resides in *******.  His mother and brother will be coming here next week for the holidays and to provide additional support to the family.  However, despite the extended family residing a distance away, both parents disclose having a lot of support from friends both in Gainesville and in ** *********.       Both parents own their own vehicle, and deny that travel to *** **** Gainesville will be problematic.       Course of illness:     ***** was diagnosed with congenital heart disease at 20 weeks gestation. The parents report that they were advised that she would likely not survive.  She was delivered by C Section at 31 weeks gestation, and immediately taken to the OR for emergency placement of epicardial wires.  She had a permanent pacemaker placed on **/*/****.  She has also had a * *** stroke.  Neurology has expressed that this is not a contra-indication to transplant, but state she will need rehab to address deficits from the stroke.                Financial Situation:     ***** is covered by her dad's **** insurance.  She has some co-pays from this.  Current co-pays for this admission are totaling about $2000.  As mom is not planning to return to work until ******, the family plans to apply for SSI to see if she might be eligible for supplemental insurance.       The family denies any financial concerns currently, but are interested in fundraising to assist with displacement expenses in the future.  SW provided information on fundraising through ****.         Family History:     There is no reported family medical history other than the paternal grandfather died from heart disease of unknown origin in his 40's.         There is no reported mental health history in the family. The family denies any substance abuse history in the family.  There is no reported history of DV or involvement with DCF.       ***** is the family's first child.  She is reported to be a carrier of CF genetically but does not have CF.     Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence noted at this time.  Both parents verbalize willingness to give meds to pt as prescribed, and verbalize feeling comfortable learning to do so. They also verbalize willingness to learn care for g-tube if pt requires that as well.  The family has also demonstrated commitment to being here for pt.  The family verbalizes a commitment to keeping follow up appointments, obtaining labs, etc.  They also verbalize a commitment to the therapies that will be needed secondary to the stroke.     Assessment and recommendations:     Although transplant was just brought up as a possibility to the family recently, both parents verbalize a willingness to pursue whatever will give ***** the best chance.  They admit that transplant is scary.  However, they state they were advised during the pregnancy that ***** would likely not survive the pregnancy.  They state they count each day as a blessing, and are hopeful that transplant may give her an even better chance at long-term survival.                       IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/ Insurance  - 1     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 1     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  1     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  9  Low     The family scores as low risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.    *Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to transplant and the extended admission         ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
